name: Derbe
overview: Derbe is a significant city in the missionary journeys of Paul and Silas, serving as a place of refuge and ministry. After facing opposition, Paul and his companions fled to Derbe, highlighting its role as a safe haven (Acts 14:6). They also visited the city to continue their work, as seen when Paul departed there with Barnabas (Acts 14:20). Additionally, Derbe is noted as the birthplace of Gaius, a fellow worker who accompanied Paul, underscoring the city's contribution to the early Christian mission (Acts 20:4). The presence of Timothy in Derbe further emphasizes its importance in the spread of the gospel (Acts 16:1).
